title: Interview Funnel Quality and Orientation Micro-Syllabus
body:
Purpose:
Standardize the interview funnel quality and create a tightly coupled mini-onboarding syllabus so that decisions at offer time map directly to day-1 priorities. This doc combines: a compact interviewer checklist and scoring rubric, interviewer calibration notes, pre-offer candidate experience timeline, and a 30/60 micro-syllabus for the first 4 weeks. Goal: reduce ramp variance, improve hiring manager satisfaction, and shorten time-to-productivity.

Scope:
Applies to technical and cross-functional hires (IC levels IC2-IC5 and equivalent managers) across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product teams. Does not replace role-specific deep onboarding plans (those live in product team folders) — this is the standardized surface-level kit used by People Ops and hiring managers.

High-level hiring goals & KPIs (recommended):
- Time-to-offer: target <= 14 days from first phone screen
- Offer acceptance rate: target >= 75% for mid-senior roles
- Hiring manager satisfaction (post-hire survey): target >= 4.2/5
- 30-day baseline task success: % of hires completing first-week deliverable >= 85%
- Ramp metric: median time to full PR/feature ownership by role band

Interview funnel quality checklist (pre-interview):
- Role brief present and up-to-date (JD + top 3 success outcomes)
- Hiring manager has completed intake form (skill priorities, unavoidable constraints)
- Interview panel finalized (no more than 6 unique interviewers across funnel)
- Candidate prep packet sent: agenda, tech requirements, interview format, example problem shapes
- Interview rubrics preloaded in Greenhouse/ATS and reviewers assigned
- Diversity-friendly scheduling rules applied (no back-to-back technical interviews without breaks)

Day-of / interviewer checklist:
- Confirm rubric and timebox with candidate at start (e.g., 60 minutes total; structure: 10m intro, 40m assessment, 10m Q&A)
- State evaluation criteria at start: clarity, problem approach, production thinking, collaboration
- Capture explicit feedback on: correctness, trade-offs, communication, ownership signals
- Avoid closed yes/no questions; favor open problems or short take-home mini-problems
- Use code/pairing environment only when candidate consents
- Report score within 24 hours; if delaying, notify People Ops and hiring manager

Scoring rubric (single page reference — 1..5 scale, per competency):
Competencies: Problem Solving, System Design (if applicable), Product Sense, Coding Correctness & Style, Communication & Collaboration, Mission/Culture Add
- 5 = Exceptional: solves with clarity, meaningful trade-offs, production-level considerations, teaches interviewer, great collaboration
- 4 = Strong: clear solution with minor gaps, pragmatic trade-offs, would ship with light review
- 3 = Solid: meets bar with noted areas to improve; needs onboarding/mentorship for gaps
- 2 = Below bar: major gaps in approach or correctness; concerns about independent delivery
- 1 = Unacceptable: inability to demonstrate core skills for the role band
Guidance: For scoring, prefer conservative rounding toward hiring manager impact; emphasize consistent application across interviewers during calibration.

Interviewer calibration notes (quarterly cadence recommended):
- 30-minute session per hiring track; sample 2 anonymized interviews and score together
- Document differences and update rubric descriptors when repeat disagreements occur
- Calibration owner: People Ops recruiter + one senior engineer from the track

Post-interview rubric synthesis and decision path:
- Collect scores and short rationale within 48 hours
- Hiring manager aggregates and writes a 1-paragraph recommendation (hire/hold/no-hire + mitigation plan for risks)
- If any reviewer gives 1-2, require a follow-up interview or cross-check with calibration panel
- People Ops triages compensation band and timeline and drafts offer language mapping top 3 outcomes

Candidate experience timeline (pre-offer):
- Day -5 to interview: send prep packet, interview agenda, main contact, and FAQ
- Day 0 (phone screen): hiring manager note with role outcomes attached
- Day 1-7: onsite/loop and feedback collection window
- Day 8-14: decision + offer creation + negotiation buffer (aim to keep under 14 days)
- Offer acceptance => start preboarding (see checklist below)

Preboarding & offer-to-start checklist (People Ops + IT + hiring manager):
- Signed offer and completed background check initiated
- New-hire welcome email with start date, first-day agenda, parking/visitor instructions
- Equipment order submitted (laptop, monitor, peripherals) with 2-week SLA for remote hires
- Access requests opened: email, Slack, GitHub, cloud console, ticketing; tag hiring manager in approvals
- Manager assigns mentor/buddy before start and schedules welcome 1:1s
- Manager provides first-week project brief at least 3 days before start

Orientation micro-syllabus (first 4 weeks — one-page, role-agnostic):
Week 0 (pre-start): read 2 short docs: company fundamentals (mission + infra stack overview) and product quick tour (10–15 min video)
Day 1: HR & security admin (AM), team welcome + intros (PM), lightweight systems orientation (how to deploy a doc, how to create a ticket). Deliverable: confirm accounts and access checklist complete.
Day 2: Team deep-dive: codebase orientation for engineers or product brief for non-engineers; pair shadowing with mentor. Deliverable: clone repo / get local dev run passing or complete product area checklist.
Day 3–5: Small onboarding ticket (owned end-to-end) that touches CI, PR process, and review flow. Deliverable: merged PR or documented blocker and next steps.
Week 2: 30-day success plan co-created with manager; identify 1 small customer-impacting task to execute by week 4.
Week 3–4: Ownership handoff and initial feature plan; manager and mentor feedback loop; first 1:1 retro at end of week 4.

First-week deliverable templates (examples):
- Backend engineer: fix a flaky test or add telemetry for an existing endpoint (small scoped PR)
- Frontend engineer: implement a tiny UI fix or add a storybook component and unit tests
- SRE/Infra: reproduce and document a standard incident runbook and run a postmortem checklist exercise
- PM/Designer: produce a one-pager scoping doc for a low-risk product change with stakeholder map

Manager commitments checklist (for hiring managers):
- Provide role outcomes and success criteria before candidate interviews begin
- Set up mentor and first-week project before start date
- Give timely feedback on interview outcomes (within 48 hours)
- Own 30/60/90 plan and review at 30-day checkpoint

Sample short handoff note (one-paragraph to drop into ATS or onboarding doc):
- Candidate: [Name], Role: [Title], Start: [Date]
- Top-3 outcomes expected in 90 days: 1) [Outcome A], 2) [Outcome B], 3) [Outcome C]
- Primary mentor: [Name], Immediate onboarding ticket: [URL/GH issue]

Evaluation & continuous improvement loop:
- Post-hire survey at 30 days for new hire + hiring manager (short 6 questions)
- Quarterly cohort review: aggregate ramp metrics and acceptance rates; identify top 2 friction points
- One experiment per quarter: e.g., adjust pre-interview packet, shorten panel, micro-assignment vs live problem; measure impact on time-to-offer and 30-day deliverable completion

Open questions / decisions for leadership:
- Do we require a live system-design stage for IC3 hires on infra-heavy teams? (recommendation: select by role, default: yes for infra/product infra tracks)
- SLA for equipment: should we aim for same-day shipping for US-based hires? (cost vs speed tradeoff)
- Should interview recordings (consent-based) be retained for calibration? (privacy/legal input needed)

Appendix: quick templates (paste-ready)
- Interviewer feedback snippet: "Candidate demonstrated X approach; strengths: A; concerns: B; recommended next step: [hire/hold/no-hire]"
- Offer note to candidate: short pitch + 3 success outcomes and manager intro
- First-week checklist link placeholder: add to team onboarding folder

Notes and provenance:
- Pulls together practices from recent hires on Platform + Serving Runtime teams (July–Oct 2025) and feedback from managers in Dedicated and Private tracks. Calibrated with Engineering recruiting leads and SRE managers.

Next steps (people-ops owners):
- Iterate on rubric language with two calibration sessions in December 2025
- Pilot micro-syllabus with 10 new hires in Q1 2026 and report ramp metrics

Document owner & contact: Leah Chen (leah.chen@redwoodinfra.com) — ping for clarifications or to propose experiments.
